alerts.title: Rising creatinine on TDF in pregnancy
alerts.message: TDF can cause renal toxicity including elevated creatinine. Patient's creatinine rose from 0.8 to 1.1 mg/dL within 10 weeks of starting TDF, and eGFR is 78 mL/min/1.73m². Pregnancy itself increases creatinine clearance and should lower creatinine, making this rise more concerning. DTG can also inhibit tubular creatinine secretion, contributing to the elevation. Against drug attribution: the urinalysis is normal with no proteinuria, and phosphate is normal, which argues against significant TDF nephrotoxicity. The eGFR of 78 may partly reflect normal pregnancy-related reference range differences. However, the upward trend warrants close monitoring.

evidence.recommended_action: Repeat creatinine and eGFR at next visit. If creatinine continues to rise or eGFR falls further, consider TDF substitution. Monitor phosphate and urinalysis concurrently.

alerts.title: DTG–iron supplement interaction in pregnancy
alerts.message: DTG requires dose separation from divalent cation-containing supplements including iron, which this pregnant patient is taking (ferrous sulfate). Guidelines specifically highlight the interaction between DTG and divalent cations in pregnancy because pregnant women frequently receive iron or calcium supplements. Co-administration without separation can reduce DTG absorption and compromise viral suppression. The patient's viral load is 89 copies/mL, which is nearly suppressed, but subtherapeutic DTG levels risk virologic failure.

evidence.recommended_action: Counsel patient to take ferrous sulfate at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after DTG. Document separation timing at next visit.

alerts.title: Missing VL monitoring plan in pregnancy
alerts.message: Guidelines specify that for ART initiated during pregnancy, a viral load should be performed at baseline and after 3 months of ART. Additionally, routine VL monitoring for pregnant and lactating women should occur every 3 months. The patient had a baseline VL of 125,000 and a VL of 89 copies/mL at approximately 10 weeks, which is appropriate. However, no clinician assessment or plan was documented today, and no follow-up VL timing is specified. Given the 3-month pregnancy monitoring interval, the next VL should be scheduled around the 6-month mark.

evidence.recommended_action: Schedule next viral load at 3 months post-initiation per pregnancy monitoring guidelines. Document a written plan for ongoing antenatal VL monitoring.

alerts.title: No clinician plan documented today
alerts.message: No assessment or plan was recorded for this visit. Guidelines require treatment monitoring including viral load at defined intervals during pregnancy, and a documented plan for ongoing care. The patient is 22 weeks pregnant on TDF/3TC/DTG with a rising creatinine trend and is taking iron supplements that interact with DTG. Absence of a documented plan risks missing these safety issues.

evidence.recommended_action: Document a comprehensive plan addressing renal monitoring, DTG-iron separation, VL scheduling, and antenatal care coordination before the patient leaves.

etween DTG and divalent cation-containing medication in pregnancy, since pregnant women frequently receive iron or calcium supplements and/or magnesium-/aluminium- containing antacids (see module 17). Patients returning to care in pregnancy after interrupting a first-line NNRTI regimen or those exposed to previous VTP regimens should be put directly on a DTG-based regimen, rather than retrying an NNRTI-regimen (see also module 16). The ACTG A5372 trial showed that DTG needs to be given twice daily for 28 days if co-administered with rifapentine. 137 Rifapentine also affects the metabolism of common ARV drugs most affected by CYP induction such as all protease inhibitors (PIs) including LPV/r, and some non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs), including nevirapine. 138 All patients receiving ART should be considered for TPT after having been screened for active TB using a symptom screen,
